quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles travel slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn carriages.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine noise and wind noise can hurt your hearing, even with a helmet on. You should wear hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position that gives you the best view and most space around you. Change your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Not required, but recommended.
Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a helmet approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, traveling in the center portion of the lane:

options.text: Allows you to be seen in its rearview mirror.
Usually makes it difficult for the driver to see you.
Should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to be seen in its rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors. This position helps them see you.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when they are riding in which lane position?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, the center position is usually best when following a car. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: When riding, sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handlebars. Press your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going forward. Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation for keeping riders together while maintaining adequate space cushions is generally:

options.text: A single-file formation.
Riding in pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of motorcycles to stay close together while giving each rider enough space around them.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: So the driver can see you in the side mirror.
So the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
So the driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself behind the vehicle in the center of your lane. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed.
How quickly the alcohol is consumed.
How often the person drinks alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how quickly it is consumed. How often someone drinks does not affect their BAC. Never ride after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight day and night when it is legal and safe. Your headlight and running lights help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Yield.
Reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you apply the rear brake, both brakes work together. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely need to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct tire pressure to use.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a road with good grip, what should you do?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks on a road with good grip, keep it locked until you stop. A locked rear wheel will not cause you to lose control as long as the motorcycle stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or people may put their arms out the window. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to operate safely.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a full-face helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down at the road surface to watch for changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: White lines and yellow lines separate traffic in different ways. What do white lines separate?

options.text: Traffic moving in the same direction.
Traffic moving in opposite directions.
Traffic and road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in which part of a lane?

options.text: The left portion
The middle portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks usually collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down while in the turn.
Turn using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: What is true about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: Use it only if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
Avoid it at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually has good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.
